answer: Black-box access allows users to design inputs for a system, query it, and analyze the resulting outputs without any insight into the internal workings of the system. In contrast, gray-box access offers users limited visibility into a system's operations, which can include information such as input embeddings, inner neuron activations, or sampling probabilities. Gray-box access provides more information than black-box access but does not grant full access to the system's internals.
